facts: axe-core 4.13.0 (WCAG 2.1 AA) reports label-content-name-mismatch (serious, WCAG 2.5.3) on the language button #language on both the home page and the product page; the button has aria-label="Select language" and its visible text is not part of that name.
axe-core reports the list rule (serious, WCAG 1.3.1) on three category <ul> elements on the home page; each directly contains a <fieldset> child, which is not an allowed child of <ul>.
The language button sits in the site-wide navigation (same element on both pages), while the list violations are in the catalog filter component, which only the home page renders.
The same violations were recorded in an earlier run (run-0669cd9d-fbd5-4ddc-8209-8102ff856471, 2026-10-22) and again in run-a3857cc2 (2026-10-26): the symptom is stable across runs.
No source code is configured for this project, so no cause was read from code.

hypotheses.description: The navigation component sets a fixed aria-label ("Select language") on a button whose visible content is the current language name or code, so the accessible name overrides and no longer contains the visible text.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: The nav component template, or a snapshot of #language showing its visible text (e.g. a language code) differing from its aria-label.

hypotheses.description: The category filter template renders each sub-category group as a <fieldset> placed directly inside a <ul> (instead of inside an <li>), for example from a loop that emits the fieldset in place of a list item.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: The filter component template, or the rendered DOM of one `.checkbox > ul` showing the fieldset's parent and sibling nodes.

remediation: Make the accessible name of #language contain its visible text: remove aria-label so the visible text names the button, or start the label with the visible text (for example 'EN, Select language'), tied to the label-content-name-mismatch fact.
Wrap each <fieldset> in a <li>, or replace the <ul> with a non-list container such as a <div>, in the category filter, tied to the list-rule fact.
Review the uncertain colour-contrast items (CO2 rating letters at about 2.3-2.8:1 and gradient/image backgrounds) manually; they are not part of this defect's confirmed violations.
regressionRecommendation: Keep a11y-catalog-and-product-pages-clean in the regression tier so it fails if either violation returns; consider adding a scan of the cart and checkout pages.
